messages:
Alex Chen: Hey team — customer hitting schema validation errors when our fn-call/toolcall returns a nested object. They included a curl repro but request_id is missing from logs, any ideas?
Ingrid Park: can you paste the curl and the error snippet? also which model + route?
Alex Chen: route: /v1/chat/completions, model: redwood/reason-v1, payload they used: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"call toolX with {\\"id\\":123}"}],"functions":[{"name":"toolX","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"result":{"type":"object","properties":{"value":{"type":"string"}}}}}}]}'```
Alex Chen: Response client saw: `400 Invalid structured output: /functions/0/parameters/result value type mismatch (expected string, got object)`
Marcus Lee: hmmm. That looks like our schema expects result.value as string but the tool returned an object. Could be serialization mismatch in the tool adapter.
Priya S.: do we have the request ID? Without it, we can't tie to logs. Alex, any headers from the curl?
Alex Chen: customer said they don't see `x-rw-request-id` in their client response. Their curl output only shows the 400 JSON body.
Ingrid Park: we should still be able to find server-side logs by time and client org. Ask for `--verbose` curl output (include headers) or have them run with `curl -i` so response headers are printed.
Alex Chen: shared short note to customer, they ran again and attached verbose output. pasted below: ```HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 18:24:16 GMT
Content-Length: 312

{"error":{"message":"Invalid structured output","type":"invalid_request_error","param":null,"code":"struct_output.invalid","meta":{"path":"/functions/0/parameters/result/value","expected":"string","received":"object"}}}```
Marcus Lee: still no x-rw-request-id header. Could the customer be hitting a proxy that strips headers?
Priya S.: also ask for the request payload (body) they sent, not the one in our sample. they might be doing nested serialization causing object->string or vice versa.
Alex Chen: customer attached the body: `{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"..."}],"functions":[{"name":"toolX","parameters":{"result":{"value":{"num":42}}}}]}`
Ingrid Park: there we go — their `result.value` is an object with `num` key, not a string. So the client-side tool (toolX) is packing a nested object. Why did it serialize that way?
Marcus Lee: possible root causes: (1) the tool's runtime emits a JSON object (intended) but our function schema expects a string; (2) our schema generation for the function was wrong (maybe used JSON pointer to the wrong path); (3) client is double-encoding.
Priya S.: can we run a local repro against the same model+route to see error formatting and whether request IDs appear? I can do a curl from our infra.
DeployBot: started job `support/repro/1782123456` on runner-3. ETA ~30s.
SentryBot: New event captured: struct_output.invalid at service=inference-runtime, env=prod, level=warning (no request_id in payload).
Marcus Lee: I'll grep logs for the timeframe and org id prefix `org_` + approx timestamp. If no request id we can still look for matching org and payload pattern.
Alex Chen: customer also said they call the tool via a wrapper that returns `toolResult` as JSON string in some cases. their wrapper code: ```js
const toolOutput = callTool();
return { result: JSON.stringify(toolOutput) }; // sometimes returns stringified object
```
Ingrid Park: that would invert expected types depending on whether the tool runtime stringifies or returns raw object. So sometimes we see an object, sometimes a string — causing validation flakiness.
Priya S.: ask customer to run a minimal curl that calls functions with the exact body they sent (not the wrapper) and include `-i` so we can get headers. Also request they add `x-rw-debug: 1` header which echoes request_id in response for debug runs (internal support feature).
Alex Chen: sent that to customer. they replied with new curl output and this header: `x-rw-request-id: req_AXY123456789`. They also included a small log snippet from their wrapper showing `JSON.stringify` usage.
Marcus Lee: got the request id — pulling logs now.
Marcus Lee: log snippet: `2026-09-21T18:24:16.432Z [info] req=req_AXY123456789 org=org_08 fn=tool-invoke payload={"name":"toolX","parameters":{"result":{"value":{}}}}`
Marcus Lee: server accepted a tool call but then validation failed downstream when matching against function parameter schema. Looks like our structured-output validator enforces `value` type per registered schema.
Ingrid Park: possible mitigation options: (A) return clearer error to customer indicating exact mismatched fragment, (B) fallback to stringifying objects when schema expects string (dangerous), (C) advise customers to ensure consistent typing in tool adapters.
Priya S.: for this case, recommend quick fix: update wrapper to always return primitives/strings for `result.value` and push a code sample. Also open an internal ticket to add a more explicit error message including `x-rw-request-id`.
Alex Chen: will send sample patch to customer and ask them to test. Also creating internal ticket: `SUP-3124` with request id and repro steps.
Marcus Lee: adding label `fncall-schema` and assigning to eng-ml to review whether schema registration produced incorrect type.
Ingrid Park: if customer prefers, we can accept a debug bundle — run `curl` with `-H 'X-RW-Debug: collect'` and upload the bundle link to the thread. Only do with consent.
Alex Chen: customer asked for an ETA. I told them I expect a quick config suggestion in 2 hours, full review in 24-48h. they replied :thumbsup:.
Priya S.: note for runbook: add a checklist item to always request `-i` output and recommend `X-RW-Debug` header.
Alex Chen: thanks all — will update thread when customer confirms patch.
Ingrid Park: nice triage, flagged follow-up for eng-ml and docs update.
DeployBot: job support/repro/1782123456 completed on runner-3 (exit=0).
Alex Chen: customer verified after changing wrapper to `result.value = String(toolOutput.num)` — now gets 200 and function call parsed correctly. Closing customer loop. :party_popper:
